title: Four-vertex lift from the exact witness ladder
novelty_claim: Treat the transition n -> n + 1 as the primary object and solve only the old-new/new-new completion problem, instead of restarting a full graph search for each target.
closest_prior_art: Local exact-witness lookup plus the negative-space note that a four-vertex lift may exist; no current repo artifact turns adjacent verified witnesses into a recursive construction program.
differentiation: This reuses the strongest verified signal already in the repo, the exact witness ladder up to n = 22, and searches a sharply restricted completion space. It avoids both Paley rehashing and full-edge stochastic search.
easiest_falsifier: Run leave-one-step-out recovery on known steps such as 20 -> 21 and 21 -> 22 with a restricted SAT/IP completion over old-new and new-new edges. If the method cannot reliably recover known next witnesses, reject it before spending budget on n = 23.
evidence_plan: Mine exact witnesses for saturated edge/non-edge pairs, degree patterns, and orbit hints.
Encode a restricted completion model that holds the old graph fixed and solves only the four added vertices and their incidences.
Benchmark recovery on known adjacent steps before attempting frontier case 22 -> 23.

budget_envelope.kill_switch: Stop after repeated failure on known-step recovery; do not escalate into unrestricted graph search.

title: Certificate-aligned pair-slack repair
novelty_claim: Optimize exact per-pair slack against the verifier's real constraints instead of surrogate bad-book counts, degree heuristics, or generic annealing scores.
closest_prior_art: The archived mixed-language local search and the bridge memo's belief-propagation repair idea.
differentiation: The baseline is not another parameter sweep on heuristic search. Every move is scored by exact edge/non-edge slack margins, with message passing allowed only after the exact-slack baseline proves it adds value.
easiest_falsifier: On n = 22, 24, and 50, compare exact max-slack repair against the old surrogate objective. If it does not improve verifier calls, best margin, or reproducibility, kill the direction.
evidence_plan: Log exact slack distributions for supported witnesses to identify the genuinely critical pairs.
Implement a bitset-backed max-slack tracker and compare it against the legacy aggregate objective.
Escalate to BP-style repair only if the exact-slack baseline beats the surrogate objective.

budget_envelope.kill_switch: Stop if the baseline collapses into ordinary heuristic tuning or shows no clear verifier-aligned gain.

title: Composite-order orbit-compressed templates
novelty_claim: Search low-orbit witnesses in cyclic or product-group templates for unsupported even and odd-composite cases, rather than stretching finite-field Paley machinery beyond its proved regime.
closest_prior_art: The known prime-power Paley-type family and the broader cyclic/block-circulant/difference-set lane flagged by the falsifier.
differentiation: The target is not 'Paley for more n'. The target is an orbit-compressed search space fitted to exact witness statistics, with composite-order templates treated as their own design objects.
easiest_falsifier: If exact witness mining does not reveal stable low-orbit or autocorrelation signatures, or if orbit-compressed SAT/ILP shows no leverage on 23, 24, or 50, reject the line.
evidence_plan: Extract orbit, autocorrelation, and degree-multiset summaries from the exact witness bank.
Fit a small family of composite-order templates and test whether they explain known witnesses better than generic circulants.
Only then spend frontier budget on 23, 24, and 50.

budget_envelope.kill_switch: Stop if the direction degenerates into cosmetic Paley variants or full graph search in disguise.
